title: Dead GCM decrypt functions with no explanation
description: In smime-tree/src/decrypt.rs, decrypt_aes128_gcm and decrypt_aes256_gcm are marked #[allow(dead_code)] but have no comment explaining why they exist. The decrypt() function above them explicitly rejects GCM-in-EnvelopedData with a note explaining it is not standard. A contributor will be confused: are these functions intended for future use (AuthEnvelopedData via RFC 5083), or are they leftover from an abandoned approach? The allow(dead_code) suppression means they will not produce a warning, so the confusion can persist indefinitely. Add a comment stating the intended future use (e.g. 'Reserved for AuthEnvelopedData (RFC 5083) support') or remove them if they are not planned.
